Four, never five. + is not a tab, because creating is not a place you go.

§1.1 · INSIGHTS ROOT · COST LENS · MONTH PAGE, TO DATE

The + is detached, and that is a doctrine not a layout

A fifth tab would make creating a place you navigate to. Instead: + creates, pencil edits, trash deletes — one icon per record type, used identically everywhere. It floats over the body on every root and opens the chooser as a fitted sheet.

Settings floats too, top-right, on every root

Not a tab, not a row inside Garage. It opens the one Settings sheet, which carries its own internal push stack. The build has no Settings surface at all today — the word appears in app/ only inside comments.

Each tab owns a stack, and leaving resets it

Coming back to History lands on History, not on a record page from last Tuesday. What survives a tab switch is screen state — the filter chips, the car scope, the lens, the page size. Resetting those would make the sacred ledger read as silently partial.

Read the bars against the headline

289,00 + 98,20 + 96,50 + 4,20 = 487,90 €. They sum to the headline exactly, and to Home's July pulse, and to History's July whisper — which is the arithmetic rule every card on every sheet obeys: a total whose parts are not all on screen is a black box.

The plan row is the whole 289,00 € because the charge is anchored to the 23rd and 23 July falls inside this partial page — not a per-day slice of it. Whether that charge is also a ledger row is §16 #13, still open. And it is named Plan, the type, never Mapfre, the brand.

Parent visible underneath. Applies on tap, closes itself, no Save button. This is the floor — nothing goes deeper.
A pushed page never dismisses itself

It pops by path mutation only. dismiss() inside a pushed page eventually rebinds to a sheet and kills Back — a hard-won bug, written down so it is not re-found.

A dirty form pins its sheet

Swipe-to-close is disabled while dirty and the sheet asks: "Discard this fill? / Keep editing". A dirty guard even wins over a notification deep-link's modal teardown — a half-typed fill is unrecoverable, a notification is still in Notification Center.

Chooser-then-sheet is not two layers

Capture's chooser is a fitted sheet that dismisses itself and then opens the task sheet. That ordering is what keeps exactly one tall layer on screen — it is a sequence, not a stack.

§1.4 · GARAGE · ZERO CARS · DARK

"No cars" and "nothing to review" are independent facts

A flag can outlive the car it was about — that is exactly what a late-child flag is. So Home keeps the row even at zero cars, and the screen must not conflate the two. History, Insights and Garage carry no such exception; their empty bodies are identical.

Zero cars wins the screen anyway

With no live car, the queue's real action — "enter it again under another car" — has nowhere honest to put the record. So Add your car to begin stays the hero and the queue gets a quiet row beneath it, not the other way round.

+ stays, and it is car-gated

Tapping it with zero cars opens the car form, not the fill-up keypad. The alternative — a disabled + — is a dead control, and the app does not scold.

One more empty state, easy to miss

A signed-in second device with no records yet must not read "Add your car to begin" — that invites the duplicate-car outcome the architecture deliberately will not auto-resolve. When sync is on and nothing has arrived, the copy is "Waiting for your records to arrive."

04 · The route map, and the one real routing problem

The current tree is a flat stack of five peer routes with the garage at the root. This is what the four-tab shell needs instead.
app/
  _layout.tsx                  Stack: (tabs) + task sheets, presentation:'modal'
  (tabs)/
    _layout.tsx                Tabs: home · history · insights · garage
    home/index.tsx             sheet 05
    history/index.tsx          batch 2
    insights/index.tsx         batch 2   ← lens + page state live here, not in the route
    garage/index.tsx           sheet 04
    garage/car/[id].tsx        sheet 04  · pushed inside Garage
    garage/car/[id]/vault.tsx  batch 2   · pushed inside Garage
    home/review/index.tsx      batch 2   · pushed inside Home
    home/reminders/index.tsx   batch 2   · pushed inside Home, off "All ›"
    record/[kind]/[id].tsx     batch 2   ← see the note
  capture/                     sheets: chooser · fuel · entry · trip · odometer
  car-form.tsx                 sheet
  reminder-form.tsx            sheet
  settings.tsx                 sheet with its OWN internal stack
  selftest.tsx                 dev-only, out of the product router

A record page is reachable from three tabs

History, a Cost-lens record row, and Home's Last-fill card all open one. Under per-tab stacks it must push inside the tab you were in — so it is one destination registered in every tab's stack, not one route owned by a tab.

Do not solve this by making records a fifth tab, and do not solve it by making them a modal. Either would break Back.

Two more need the same treatment

The vault is reached only from the Garage tab's car page, so it is a normal single-tab push. The reminder detail is reached from both Home's All › and the car page's Care group — so it needs the shared-destination treatment too, not a route owned by either tab.

What the shell needs that does not exist yet

An app-level toast host — one at a time is currently true only per screen, across three separate mounts, which is why a car delete has to smuggle its message through a route param. Plus swipeable rows and the sheet dirty guard: both gesture libraries are installed and imported nowhere.

Sheet 03 of 08. Next: 04 Garage and the car page — the two surfaces whose data already exists, and the two carrying the live contradictions, so they are where these wireframes get their first real test.
